title: Veterans Pension One-Time Payment Declarations — Period Covered
content:
# Period covered by a one-time payment declaration (Veterans Pension)

The period a Veterans Pension one-time payment declaration covers follows the award — the pension effective date, and any one-time declaration already received on the award. Every month count runs to the declaration — the day the veteran files it, not the date the declaration carries:

1. When the pension award took effect fewer than 12 whole months before the declaration, only releases deposited in the whole months since the pension effective date are declared.
2. When the award is older and a one-time declaration was already received in the 12 whole months before, only releases deposited since that declaration are declared — the whole months since the most recent such declaration was received.
3. Otherwise the 12 whole months before the declaration are covered.

## Decision table

| Award age (whole months since the pension effective date) | One-time declaration received in the 12 whole months before | Period covered |
|---|---|---|
| fewer than 12 | — | the whole months since the pension effective date |
| 12 or more | yes | the whole months since that declaration |
| 12 or more | no | the 12 whole months before the declaration |

## Boundary illustrations (hypothetical)

- Award effective 11 whole months ago: releases deposited in those 11 months are declared.
- Award effective 12 whole months ago, no earlier declaration in that time: the 12 whole months are covered.
- Award effective 30 whole months ago, a one-time declaration received 5 whole months ago: only releases deposited in the 5 whole months since are declared.
